Pseudotime analysis showed dynamic changes in representative gene expression, indicating transcriptional state variation.
CONCLUSION: The complex immune response in the ESCC microenvironment is revealed in this study through the exploration of immune cells and key gene activity at single-cell transcriptional resolution. This knowledge may help guide the development of personalized immunotherapies by revealing the roles of specific immune cells and potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Exploration of neuroimmune and brain network mechanisms of Jin's three-needle therapy in promoting ischemic stroke recovery: a randomized controlled trial protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional impairment during the recovery phase of ischemic stroke (IS) substantially diminishes patients' long-term quality of life. Although rehabilitation therapy promotes functional recovery, some patients still face persistent functional limitations, underscoring the need for effective adjuvant interventions. Acupuncture is widely used in stroke rehabilitation, and Jin's three-needle therapy has shown potential benefits for post-stroke motor dysfunction. However, high-quality randomized controlled trial evidence regarding its clinical efficacy and neuroimmunomodulatory mechanisms remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of Jin's three-needle therapy for functional impairment during the recovery phase of ischemic stroke, and to explore potential associations between brain functional network changes and peripheral immune alterations using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) and immune marker assessments.
METHODS: This randomized, controlled, assessor-blinded trial will enroll 70 patients with ischemic stroke in the recovery phase from The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either Jin's three-needle therapy or non-penetrating sham acupuncture, while both groups receive the same standardized conventional rehabilitation and guideline-based basic treatment. The intervention will be administered for 3 weeks (5 treatment days per week). Treatment providers will not be blinded, whereas patients, outcome assessors, and data analysts will remain blinded. The primary outcome is the change in the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score. Secondary outcomes include the Modified Barthel Index (MBI) and modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Exploratory outcomes include peripheral immune-related markers, including regulatory T cell proportion, CD39 expression on Tregs, plasma plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) levels, and rs-fMRI-based functional connectivity changes. Associations among changes in clinical outcomes, brain functional connectivity, and peripheral biomarkers will be explored. Follow-up assessments will be conducted at 1 and 3 months after discharge.
DISCUSSION: This study integrates clinical assessments, peripheral biomarker measurements, and brain functional imaging to investigate the multidimensional effects of Jin's three-needle therapy on functional impairment during the recovery phase of ischemic stroke. The findings may provide objective evidence for evaluating this therapy and characterize treatment-associated changes in peripheral immune-related biomarkers and brain functional connectivity, as well as their associations with clinical recovery.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/mgt/search, identifier ITMCTR2026001598.

articles.title: SIM0278, an IL-2 mutein that selectively expands regulatory T cells for the treatment of autoimmune disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are essential for maintaining immune tolerance, and their dysfunction contributes to autoimmune diseases. Interleukin-2 (IL-2)-based therapies aiming to expand Tregs are limited by a short half-life and broad immune activation. This study aims to develop a long-acting IL-2 variant with enhanced Treg selectivity for the treatment of autoimmune diseases.
METHODS: Using a computation-driven protein engineering strategy, we designed an optimized IL-2 mutein to attenuate binding to IL-2 receptor (IL-2R) βγ while preserving high-affinity engagement with IL-2Rαβγ. The mutein was fused to a human Fc fragment to generate SIM0278. Its receptor binding profile, downstream signaling, and cellular selectivity were characterized in vitro. In vivo pharmacodynamics and therapeutic efficacy were evaluated in healthy mice, multiple autoimmune disease models and cynomolgus monkeys.
RESULTS: Compared with wild type IL-2, SIM0278 maintained comparable activity toward IL-2Rαβγ while showing reduced activity toward IL-2Rβγ. This receptor response profile translated into preferential STAT5 activation in Tregs, with substantially reduced activation of conventional T cells and CD8+ T cells. In healthy mice, SIM0278 potently expanded Tregs. In models of delayed-type hypersensitivity, atopic dermatitis, graft-versus-host disease, and systemic lupus erythematosus, SIM0278 demonstrated robust, dose-dependent therapeutic effects, reducing inflammation, autoantibody production, and mortality. In cynomolgus monkeys, SIM0278 showed prolonged half-life with sustained and selective Treg expansion.
CONCLUSION: SIM0278 is a selective and long-acting Treg-biased IL-2 mutein fusion protein with promising therapeutic potential for various autoimmune diseases.

articles.title: Single-Cell and Transcriptomic Analyses Identify the Regulatory T Cell-Associated Gene MED10 as a Prognostic Predictor in Colorectal Cancer.
articles.abstract: NA: Tregs significantly shape the colorectal cancer (CRC) immune microenvironment, yet the roles of specific Treg-associated genes remain poorly understood. Treg-related genes were screened from scRNA-seq data (GSE161277), followed by expression and prognostic validation in several independent cohorts (TCGA, GSE87211, GSE44076, and GSE17538). GSEA and CellChat characterized regulatory pathways and intercellular communication. MED10 expression was verified in CRC tissues and cell lines by qRT-PCR and western blotting. Functional assays (CCK-8, colony formation, wound healing, flow cytometry) evaluated MED10's impact on tumor behavior. Finally, the in vivo relevance of MED10 to tumor growth and immune microenvironmental changes was assessed using a syngeneic mouse model. MED10 was identified as a critical Treg-related gene in CRC, with high expression correlating with shortened survival. GSEA revealed that high MED10 expression was associated with enrichment of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Furthermore, intercellular communication analysis suggested that elevated MED10 expression may be associated with increased interaction strengths between cell populations, potentially contributing to the remodeling of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In vitro functional assays revealed that MED10 knockdown significantly impaired CRC cell proliferation and migration while inducing apoptosis. MED10 knockdown also reduced Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity, which was partially restored by LiCl treatment. Finally, in vivo, MED10 silencing suppressed tumor growth and was accompanied by reduced Treg infiltration and enhanced effector T-cell activity. MED10 is associated with CRC progression, Wnt/β-catenin signaling alterations, and a Treg-enriched immunosuppressive immune context, supporting its potential value as a prognostic indicator and candidate therapeutic target.

articles.title: Modified Fangji Huangqi Decoction ameliorates IgA nephropathy by enriching Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans to rebalance Th17/Treg.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormalities in mucosal immunity caused by gut microbiota dysbiosis are one of the key factors in the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Modified Fangji Huangqi Decoction (MFHD) is an effective treatment for IgAN, but it remains unclear whether its therapeutic effect is mediated by modulating the gut microbiota and thereby influencing mucosal immunity.
METHODS: The chemical composition of MFHD was analyzed using UPLC-MS/MS. The renoprotective effects of different doses of MFHD on IgAN mice were evaluated by examining renal pathology and laboratory parameters. Additionally, a combination of metagenomics, flow cytometry, ELISA, and Western blot techniques was used to evaluate the effects of MFHD on the gut microbiota-mucosal immune axis. Potential functional bacterial species were identified through correlation analysis, and their effects were validated through strain transplantation experiments in a pseudo-germ-free mouse model.
RESULTS: MFHD reduces urinary protein and improves renal pathological damage in IgAN mice. MFHD significantly increases gut microbiota diversity, enriches beneficial bacteria, and reverses the Th17/Treg immune imbalance, thereby reducing IgA+ plasma cells and serum IgA and IgG levels. Correlation analyses and strain transplantation experiment further confirmed that intestinal colonization by Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans restores the Th17/Treg balance and inhibits the differentiation of IgA+ plasma cells, thereby exerting a renoprotective effect. Additionally, both MFHD and Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans increase the expression of occludin and ZO-1, thereby improving histopathological damage in the small intestine.
CONCLUSION: MFHD improves IgAN by regulating the gut microbiota-particularly by enriching Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans-thereby restoring the Th17/Treg immune balance and reducing IgA secretion.

articles.title: Regulatory T and Activated T Cells in the Chronic Unpredictable Mild Stress Mice: Sex Differences and Effects of Treatments.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with immune dysregulation, including T-cell activation and reduced regulatory T cells. Pharmacological treatments like fluoxetine, simvastatin, curcumin, and S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe) show promise in alleviating depressive symptoms, but their effects on immune responses are not fully understood.
METHODS: This study explored immune status in MDD using the chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model. It examined how fluoxetine, simvastatin, curcumin, and SAMe affected immune responses and depressive behaviors. The study also investigated sex differences. Six groups, each with 12 mice (6 males and 6 females), were included: control, CUMS and drug treatments. Male and female mice were housed separately in sex-specific cages throughout the experiment, with three mice per cage. Behavioral tests included sucrose preference, forced swimming, open field and active avoidance. Immune cell markers were analyzed by flow cytometry.
RESULTS: CUMS mice showed immune imbalance, with Treg depletion (p = 0.047) and a higher CD154/CD152 ratio (p = 0.006). All treatments improved depressive-like behaviors (all p < 0.05), with SAMe normalizing the CD154/CD152 ratio (p = 0.009). Furthermore, female mice exhibited lower levels of Treg-related immune regulation and T-cell activation compared to males (both p < 0.001), along with a higher CD154/CD152 ratio (p = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: This study highlights that curcumin, simvastatin, fluoxetine, and SAMe alleviate depressive-like behaviors, while SAMe also reduces the CD154/CD152 ratio. These findings reveal marked sex differences in T-cell activation and immune regulation, highlighting the importance of considering sex as a biological variable in CUMS research.

articles.title: Disarming Tumor-Protective Tregs by Targeting Heparanase 1.
Heparanase-Expressing Regulatory T Cells Drive Immunotherapy Resistance and Poor Outcomes in Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: NA: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs) and their degrading enzyme heparanase (Hpse) play pivotal roles in tumor invasion and metastasis. Previous studies have reported associations between Hpse expression in tumor cells and patient prognosis. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are a cornerstone of solid tumor therapy, the role of Hpse in antitumor immunity remains unclear. Here, we examined Hpse localization and its impact on the immune microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma. To investigate the relationships among the Hpse expression, tumor prognosis, and tumor-infiltration of immune cells, an immunohistochemical analysis of Hpse1, Hpse2, regulatory T cells (Tregs), macrophages, and CD8+ T cells was performed in resected tumor tissue from lung adenocarcinoma patients. The effects of the Hpse inhibitor PG545 on the invasive capabilities of lymphocytes were investigated. In lung adenocarcinoma tissues, Hpse1 and Hpse2 were expressed in both epithelial tumor cells and immune cells. A high Hpse1 expression and low Hpse2 expression are poor postoperative prognostic factors in both epithelial cells and tumor-infiltrating hematopoietic cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing of human tumor-infiltrating immune cells revealed that Tregs and some subclusters of macrophages specifically express Hpse1. Lung adenocarcinoma tissue with high Hpse-expressing immune cells demonstrated an increase in tumor-infiltrating Tregs. PG545 suppressed the invasion of Tregs toward the HSPG-containing ECM. Furthermore, PG545 suppressed tumor progression and infiltration of Tregs in a mouse model. In addition, PG545 reinforced antitumor effects of PD-L1 blockade. Hpse expression in Tregs has a significant impact on lung cancer progression and is a promising therapeutic target for novel combination immunotherapy.

articles.title: Baseline immune profiles are associated with positive outcomes in young children with a peanut allergy, enrolled in a randomised clinical trial for oral immunotherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peanut allergy affects around 3% of Australian infants, can cause life-threatening anaphylactic reactions and often persists throughout life. Oral immunotherapy (OIT) is a promising treatment to achieve desensitisation, but treatment outcomes vary. This study describes the immunological profiles associated with favourable OIT outcomes.
METHODS: This study assessed blood samples from 49 peanut-allergic children (1-4 years old) who participated in the Early Peanut Immunotherapy in Children (EPIC) randomised controlled trial. Children randomised to undergo peanut OIT (n = 24), or to follow the current recommended clinical practise of strict peanut avoidance (n = 25) for twelve months, were immunologically evaluated. Desensitisation outcomes were assessed using an end of treatment (EOT) oral food challenge, and blood samples were collected at baseline, 12-week follow-up (OIT only), and EOT. Thirty immune cell subsets were identified using an established immune cell flow cytometry panel and an FcεR1 expression panel.
RESULTS: As part of the clinical trial, OIT induced either partial or complete desensitisation in 91.3% of participants in the intervention group, compared to 20.8% in the avoidance group. After 12 weeks of treatment, OIT-treated patients displayed an expansion of basophils, monocytes and dendritic cells compared to levels at recruitment. At EOT, OIT increased the abundance of CD4- T effector memory cells and mast cell progenitors. Younger children with low levels of peanut-specific IgE were more likely to achieve complete desensitisation. Such outcome was also associated with low levels of CD4+ memory Tregs and CD4- central memory T cells at recruitment, whereas increased levels of basophils were associated with partial desensitisation. Differences between partial and complete desensitisation were also observed regarding dendritic cell activation and expression of the IgE receptor.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that immune signatures vary according to OIT clinical response and may have utility in monitoring treatment progress and in identifying children most likely to benefit from OIT in the future.
articles.journal: Allergy, asthma, and clinical immunology : official journal of the Canadian Society of Allergy and Clinical Immunology

articles.title: Pathomics-based prediction of natural regulatory T cell infiltration in breast cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Natural regulatory T cells (nTregs) are a key immunosuppressive component of the tumor microenvironment (TME), but their assessment typically requires specialized molecular assays. This study aimed to develop and validate a deep learning-based pathomics model to predict nTregs infiltration directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole slide images (WSI) of breast cancer and evaluate its prognostic significance.
METHODS: Data from 1097 breast cancer patients in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed. A cohort of 928 patients with complete RNA-seq data was used to establish the prognostic value of nTregs (estimated by ImmuneCellAI). A subset of 791 patients with matched high-quality H&E-stained WSI was randomly split into training (n = 633) and validation (n = 158) cohorts. A total of 1488 quantitative pathomic features were extracted. After feature selection via minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), a Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) classifier was trained to predict high versus low nTregs status, generating a continuous Pathomics Score (PS). The PS was validated against FOXP3 immunohistochemistry (IHC) and evaluated for its association with overall survival (OS). Multi-omics analyses explored the underlying biology of PS-defined groups.
RESULTS: High nTregs infiltration was an independent predictor of poor OS (HR = 1.58, 95% CI 1.10-2.28, p = 0.013). The GBM model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.81 (95% CI 0.78-0.85) in the training cohort and 0.72 (95% CI 0.63-0.80) in the validation cohort. The PS showed a strong correlation with FOXP3+ cell density (p < 0.001) and was independently associated with worse OS (HR = 1.68, 95% CI 1.15-2.46, p = 0.008). Patients with high PS exhibited a distinct transcriptomic signature enriched for immune activation pathways (e.g., estrogen responses) and upregulated immune checkpoint genes (e.g., CD276, TNFSF4, TNFSF9), alongside an immunosuppressive microenvironment characterized by increased nTregs and M2-like macrophage estimates.
CONCLUSION: We developed and validated a pathomics model that non-invasively predicts nTregs infiltration and patient prognosis from standard H&E images. The PS serves as a novel, accessible digital biomarker that captures the complexity of an inflamed yet immunosuppressive TME and has the potential to augment clinical decision-making, particularly in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: The immune microenvironment in MDS-to-AML transformation: dynamic ecological remodeling and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: NA: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) are clonal myeloid neoplasms characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis, cytopenias, and a variable risk of transformation to Acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Although genetic lesions are central to MDS pathogenesis, progression to AML cannot be explained by mutation accumulation alone. This review synthesizes evidence that MDS-to-AML transformation is a dynamic ecological process driven by reciprocal interactions between mutant hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell clones and the bone marrow immune microenvironment. In normal marrow, hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, T cells, NK(natural killer) cells, myeloid cells, mesenchymal stromal cells, endothelial cells, and the extracellular matrix maintain hematopoietic homeostasis and immune surveillance. In MDS, chronic inflammation coexists with impaired immune effector function, including T-cell exhaustion, reduced NK-cell cytotoxicity, expansion of myeloid-derived suppressor cells and immunosuppressive regulatory T-cell subsets, monocyte-macrophage reprogramming, mesenchymal stromal cell dysfunction, extracellular matrix remodeling, and metabolic adaptation. Together, these alterations establish a proinflammatory but immunosuppressive niche that weakens clearance of abnormal clones while providing stromal and metabolic support for clonal expansion and treatment resistance. Mutant clones further remodel the niche through epigenetic silencing, altered chemokine and cytokine signaling, and inflammatory-metabolic reprogramming, generating positive-feedback circuits that link inflammation, DNA damage, immune escape, increasing clonal burden, and therapy resistance. This review discusses how integrating clonal genetics with immune, stromal, and metabolic features may refine risk stratification and inform microenvironment-directed combination therapies. Longitudinal single-cell and spatial profiling will be essential for identifying reversible immune dysfunction and developing individualized strategies to delay or prevent AML transformation.

articles.title: Ultrasound-targeted nanobubble destruction induces Macro Ccl8 to suppress treg function and enhance immunotherapy efficacy in CRC.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) is largely resistant to immune checkpoint blockade due to its immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Ultrasound-targeted nanobubble destruction (UTND) offers a localized physical delivery method, but its active immunomodulatory mechanisms remain underexplored.
METHODS: Ultrasound-responsive NBs loaded with CTLA-4 antibody (PF4) were fabricated and characterized. A CT26 mouse CRC model was used to evaluate anti-tumor effects across four treatment groups. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analyzed cellular changes in the TME. The activation of the NF-κB pathway was verified through western blot analysis, qPCR, and immunofluorescence staining. Intracellular ROS production was assessed using flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, and an enzyme immunoassay. Furthermore, the effects of Ccl8 on regulatory T (Treg) cells were examined by flow cytometry, qPCR and western blot.
RESULTS: Combination treatment with UTND and anti-CTLA-4 suppressed tumor growth relative to single-agent treatments. ScRNA-seq identified a CCL8-expressing macrophage subpopulation (Macro Ccl8) that was more abundant in the combination group. UTND promoted ROS production, which activated NF-κB signaling and increased Ccl8 transcription. CCL8 secreted by Macro Ccl8 modulated Treg function through the Ccl8-Ccr2 axis. Together with direct CTLA-4 checkpoint inhibition, this cascade contributed to elevated CD8 + T cell activity.
CONCLUSIONS: In the CT26 mouse model, UTND combined with CTLA-4 antibody modulates the immunosuppressive TME partially through inducing Macro Ccl8 via the ROS-NF-κB-Ccl8 axis, in addition to direct CTLA-4 blockade. This dual mechanism attenuates Treg function and enhances antitumor immunity, providing a preclinical rationale for combining ultrasound-based physical intervention with immunotherapy in MSS CRC.

articles.title: Genetic analyses prioritize a candidate peripheral ferroptosis-related immune-protein network in migraine.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Migraine is a disabling neurological disorder with substantial clinical heterogeneity. Ferroptosis-annotated genes encompass functions related to iron and redox homeostasis, lipid peroxidation, and immune regulation, but the genetically supported relationships connecting these processes with peripheral immune-cell phenotypes and circulating proteins have not been systematically examined.
METHODS: We integrated summary-data-based Mendelian randomization, two-sample Mendelian randomization, colocalization analysis, indirect-effect analysis, PBMC single-cell RNA sequencing, and druggability annotation. Five migraine genome-wide association study datasets were analyzed; GCST90043743 included 166 cases and was treated as a sensitivity dataset. A set of 718 ferroptosis-related genes was evaluated using blood mQTL and eQTL resources and plasma pQTL datasets, while immune-cell MR included 731 immunophenotypes. Evidence was first assessed across molecular data types and migraine outcomes and was then integrated with immune-cell traits, circulating proteins, single-cell expression context, and druggability information.
RESULTS: Thirteen genes met the highest cross-omics evidence criteria: ACADSB, ADAMTS13, CDH1, CHMP1A, DPP4, GCH1, GSTM1, ISCU, MAPK9, MAPK14, MUC1, TFRC, and TLR4. A further 25 genes showed recurrent but incomplete cross-omics evidence. Of 2,087 colocalization tests, 313 met the colocalization support criterion, and all 13 highest-evidence genes had at least one result meeting this criterion. Immune-cell MR identified recurrent CD27-related B-cell and CD33-related myeloid traits. Thirty-four matched results from the two indirect-effect analyses were retained; 22 shared CD27-related B-cell traits between GSTM1- or TFRC-related gene-side results and ENPP2-related protein-side results. Additional matched results involved MUC1, myeloid dendritic-cell or naive CD8bright T-cell traits, and HMOX1 or IDO1; ALOX15, CD38-related B-cell or activated Treg traits, and IL1B; and CISD2, a CD27-related B-cell trait, and IFNG. PBMC single-cell RNA sequencing provided peripheral cell-type expression context, and targeted pseudobulk analysis showed increased IFNG expression in CD8+ T cells after Bonferroni correction. Druggability annotation highlighted ENPP2, IDO1, IL1B, and IFNG for translational follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: This study prioritizes a candidate peripheral ferroptosis-related immune-protein network associated with migraine susceptibility. The most recurrent relationship involved GSTM1 or TFRC, CD27-related B-cell traits, and ENPP2, with additional myeloid, B-cell/Treg, and inflammatory components. These findings nominate genetically informed candidates for biomarker research, immune-metabolic stratification, and experimental target investigation in migraine.
articles.journal: The journal of headache and pain

articles.title: Promoting anti-tumor immune response in osteosarcoma by BETi through restoring Th17/Treg balance.
articles.abstract: NA: The immune landscape of osteosarcoma (OS) remains incompletely characterized. We examined the Th17/Treg balance using public single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets, multiplex immunohistochemistry, peripheral-blood flow cytometry, an exploratory xenogeneic mouse model, and mechanistic assays. Human datasets and specimens were consistent with a Treg-enriched, lower Th17/Treg immune state, with the most pronounced imbalance in the peripheral blood of patients with metastatic disease. In the mouse model, BET inhibitor (BETi) treatment produced parameter-specific attenuation of osteolytic changes and shifts in Th17 and Treg frequencies. BRD4 chromatin-occupancy, expression, and migration assays identified the CXCL12/CXCR4 pathway as a candidate mechanism. B7-H3 was elevated in metastatic OS in the analyzed cohort, but none of the evaluated checkpoint-associated genes was significantly associated with overall survival. Under the tested schedules, full-dose BETi produced the greatest overall improvement in observed survival time and tumor-burden measures; the reduced-dose BETi and anti-B7-H3 combination remained active but did not outperform BETi monotherapy. These findings support that BRD4 can serve as a potential therapeutic target for OS to reverse its immunosuppressive microenvironment, and further in-depth research is warranted.

articles.title: Pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for systemic immune modulation in diabetes therapy.
articles.abstract: NA: Embryonic development is characterized by remarkable immune tolerance, yet whether this property extends to pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) has remained unclear. Here we show that EVs from pluripotent stem cells (PSCs), including embryonic stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cells, outperform mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs in suppressing proinflammatory cytokine secretion, reducing T cell activation and inducing regulatory T cells. PSC EVs display distinct molecular signatures, containing unique proteins and microRNAs absent from mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs, including the pluripotency-associated proteins ROR1 and CD133 and members of the miR-302 family. Dynamic suspension culture of PSC aggregates enhances the EV yield, providing a scalable and reproducible source. Delivered via a biomaterial scaffold, two local injections of induced PSC EVs significantly improved diabetes-free survival in an antigen-specific type 1 diabetes model, increasing regulatory T cell populations in draining lymph nodes, as well as inducing systemic immune modulation and preserving β-cell mass. These findings establish PSC EVs as a scalable immunomodulatory platform for autoimmune disease and for immune tolerance in cell therapy.

articles.title: Sexual exposure to HIV-1 is associated with lower systemic inflammation and differential activation of CD8+, CD4+, and regulatory T cells in blood and genital mucosa.
articles.abstract: NA: A continued challenge for the development of efficacious HIV-1 vaccines is the lack of detailed knowledge of immune correlates of exposure or protection. Studies of HIV-1 exposed seronegative individuals (HESN) have been conducted in attempts to define host strategies to prevent infection upon natural HIV-1 exposure. Here, we utilized blood and cervicovaginal tissue samples collected from a cohort of heterosexual Kenyan couples wherein we compared HIV-seronegative women who were HIV-1-exposed or HIV-1-unexposed to characterize in detail the circulating and genital mucosal immune landscape associated with HIV-1 sexual exposure. HIV-1 exposure was associated with significantly lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in serum without significant differences in the cervicovaginal fluid. Further, sexual HIV-1 exposure was associated with lower frequencies of activated circulating CD8 T cells yet higher levels of circulating conventional CD4 T cells expressing Ki67, a marker of recent proliferation. Finally, we report that HIV-1 exposure was associated with higher expression of immunosuppressive, migration, and proliferation markers by cervical tissue and circulating regulatory T cells. Overall, we demonstrate signatures indicating the possibility of both active immune surveillance and immunoregulation in circulation and genital tissues upon sexual HIV-1 exposure and highlight the importance of investigating T cell responses across relevant anatomic sites.

articles.title: Enhancing TCR-T cell responses with a TGFβ-specific chimeric antigen receptor.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overcoming the suppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) remains an important unmet challenge for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapies. Transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) is a key driver of T-cell suppression, reducing T-cell receptor (TCR)-mediated cytotoxicity and driving the differentiation of immunosuppressive regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the TME.
METHODS: To overcome TGFβ-mediated immunosuppression, we employed a TGFβ-targeting CAR coexpressed with a human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) E711-19-specific, HLA-A*02:01-restricted TCR (E7 TCR) in T cells. TGFβ-CAR constructs incorporating either CD28 or 4-1BB costimulatory domains were evaluated for their effects on T-cell function and phenotype.
RESULTS: Compared with T cells expressing E7 TCR only or E7 TCR with an irrelevant CD19 CAR, T cells co-transduced with E7 TCR and TGFβ-CAR showed enhanced proliferation and cytokine production while maintaining cytotoxicity upon repeated rounds of challenge with HPV16+ Ca Ski tumor cells, which provided a natural source of active TGFβ in coculture. TGFβ-CAR-expressing T cells also exhibited reduced exhaustion-marker expression and Treg differentiation after repeated antigen challenges. Transcriptional analysis further showed reduced FOXP3 expression and enhanced expression of proinflammatory genes including IFNG. In mice bearing B16-F10 tumors, TGFβ-BB-ζ-expressing pmel-1 cells reduced tumor burden and prolonged progression-free survival versus PBS and increased circulating donor T cells versus mock-transduced controls.
CONCLUSIONS: Together, these data demonstrate that TGFβ-CAR can enhance T-cell effector function while limiting Treg differentiation, supporting its development as a platform to improve the function and persistence of TCR-T cell therapies in suppressive TMEs.

articles.title: PIKFYVE inhibition alters lysosomal, mitochondrial and redox homeostasis and promotes Foxp3+ cell generation under Th17-polarizing conditions.
articles.abstract: NA: PIKFYVE, a lipid kinase that generates the endolysosomal phosphoinositide PI(3,5)P2, has emerged as a regulator of Th17 lineage commitment, but how lysosomal phosphoinositide signaling relates to mitochondrial redox homeostasis and T cell epigenetic programming is unknown. Using quantitative proteomics and pharmacological PIKFYVE inhibition with apilimod in Th17-polarized CD4+ T cells, we found that PIKFYVE inhibition reduced IL-17+ cells and increased Foxp3+ cell generation, accompanied by changes in lysosomal, mitochondrial, and redox homeostasis. Proteomics showed higher levels of endolysosomal trafficking, lysosomal acidification, and autophagy proteins and lower levels of glycolytic enzymes. PIKFYVE inhibition lowered the mitochondrial fusion proteins OPA1 and MFN2 and raised respiratory-chain protein content, oxygen consumption, mitochondrial membrane potential, and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), whereas intracellular ATP was lower. Lysosomal enlargement, higher LC3-II and p62, and lower PINK1 and Parkin suggest impaired organelle turnover that may contribute to the retention of hyperpolarized mitochondria. Higher ROS coincided with lower ATP citrate lyase (ACLY) abundance, less non-oxidized ACLY and STAT3, lower expression of Th17-associated genes, and reduced H3K27 acetylation, which N-acetylcysteine (NAC) partially restored. NAC strongly reduced Foxp3+ cell generation, including the increase induced by PIKFYVE inhibition. Similar mitochondrial, lysosomal, and redox changes were detected in CD4+ T cells from mice with experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), supporting their in vivo relevance. These findings associate PIKFYVE inhibition with altered lysosomal, mitochondrial, and redox homeostasis and a shift from Th17 toward regulatory T (Treg) cells.

articles.title: Montelukast attenuates experimental food allergy and reduces colonic eosinophilic inflammation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Montelukast, a cysteinyl leukotriene receptor antagonist, may modulate eosinophilic inflammation and immune regulation in food allergy, but its effects in intestinal allergic inflammation remain unclear.
METHODS: The effects of pre-challenge montelukast administration were evaluated in an ovalbumin-induced mouse model of food allergy. Mice were assigned to Control, montelukast-treated, ovalbumin-sensitized, and montelukast-treated ovalbumin-sensitized groups. Allergic responses, serum ovalbumin-specific immunoglobulin E, colonic eosinophil infiltration, Foxp3 expression, and epithelial adhesion proteins were assessed.
RESULTS: Time-point specific comparisons showed lower anaphylaxis scores and a smaller reduction in rectal temperature in the ML+OVA group than in the OVA group at selected post challenge time points. Montelukast also reduced colonic eosinophilic infiltration in ovalbumin-sensitized mice. Colonic Foxp3 protein expression was increased, whereas Foxp3 immunohistochemical staining showed no statistically significant difference between the ovalbumin and montelukast-treated ovalbumin groups. Montelukast did not restore the ovalbumin-associated reduction in E-cadherin expression, although N-cadherin expression tended to be lower after treatment. In exploratory correlation analyses of data pooled across all experimental groups, eosinophil infiltration and E-cadherin expression showed opposing associations with allergic symptom severity.
CONCLUSION: Pre-challenge montelukast administration attenuated experimental food-allergic responses, primarily in association with reduced colonic eosinophilic inflammation. Although colonic Foxp3 protein expression increased, Foxp3 immunohistochemical staining did not differ significantly between the OVA and ML+OVA groups; therefore, these findings do not establish a change in Treg abundance or function.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology

articles.title: Interleukin-6 and the maternal-placental immune axis in preeclampsia: from implantation to postpartum cardiovascular disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and is increasingly understood as a disorder of maternal-fetal immune maladaptation, in which interleukin-6 (IL-6) occupies a central position. IL-6 is usually examined at a single disease stage, which obscures its role as a continuous mediator.
CONTENT: This narrative review traces IL-6 across the preeclampsia continuum: signalling biology; the decidual immune niche; the regulatory T-cell/T-helper-17 and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 axes; defective placentation; antiangiogenic endothelial injury; the clinical phenotype; postpartum inflammation; and remote cardiovascular disease. Evidence is labelled by provenance, the roles of IL-6 as biomarker, mediator and therapeutic target are distinguished, and aspirin, heparin and IL-6-directed therapies are appraised.
SUMMARY: IL-6 links immune-tolerance failure to angiogenic imbalance and endothelial dysfunction, and altered inflammatory profiles persist years after delivery. Causal evidence, however, rests largely on animal and in vitro work; human data are associative and confounded by shared cardiometabolic risk; and the first large trial of IL-6 ligand inhibition lowered inflammation without reducing cardiovascular events.
OUTLOOK: Longitudinal, signalling-specific measurement, explicit separation of marker from mediator and target, and safety-led evaluation in pregnancy are required before this axis can inform prevention or postpartum cardiovascular risk stratification.

articles.title: The Role of Ginsenoside Rg3 in Cancer Treatment and the Regulation of the Tumor Immune Microenvironment.
articles.abstract: NA: The therapeutic paradigm for solid tumors is shifting toward comprehensive interventions targeting the tumor microenvironment (TME). Ginsenoside Rg3, a bioactive monomer derived from Panax ginseng, exhibits potent immunomodulatory potential. However, its clinical application is hindered by poor aqueous solubility, intestinal microbial metabolism, and variable systemic exposure. This review critically evaluates the preclinical and clinical evidence of Rg3 across solid tumors-including lung, breast, and liver cancers, and melanoma-focusing on its multidimensional remodeling of the TME. At the molecular level, Rg3 suppresses oncogenic signaling (STAT3, PI3K, and NF-κB) and downregulates immunosuppressive cytokines (IL-6, IL-10, and TGF-β) and chemokines (CCL3/4/5), while inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD) and upregulating IFN-γ and IL-2. At the cellular level, in selected preclinical models, Rg3 and Rg3-containing formulations altered macrophage polarization and other immune-associated responses and enhanced T-cell responses and NK-cell cytotoxicity. Concurrently, it impedes the recruitment of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs). Furthermore, Rg3 regulates the HIF-1α/VEGF axis to modulate hypoxia-associated signaling. To overcome its pharmacokinetic limitations, nanocarrier delivery systems are discussed as investigational strategies. Ultimately, Rg3 warrants further investigation as an adjunct to cancer therapy, although its immunotherapeutic value remains to be established.

articles.title: Linked suppression in transplantation: mechanistic boundaries and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Linked suppression is often used to explain how antigen-specific regulatory T cells (Tregs) might control a complex, multivalent alloimmune response. This review separates linked suppression from bystander suppression and infectious tolerance and considers how direct, indirect, and semi-direct allorecognition define the antigen-presenting cell (APC) substrate on which it can occur.
RECENT FINDINGS: Classic transplantation models showed that regulation directed to one antigen can restrain responses to additional antigens when they are physically linked within a graft or presented by the same APC. The breadth and mechanism may vary with donor-antigen burden and the degree of HLA sharing. Relevant interactions appear concentrated in the graft and draining lymph nodes rather than peripheral blood. CTLA-4-dependent B7 removal, local adenosine generation, and spatial organization within APC-rich niches are plausible mechanisms. Small-animal islet, minor-antigen-mismatch, and TCR-transgenic models provide tools to test these variables. Early clinical studies establish feasibility but do not yet prove linked suppression in humans.
SUMMARY: Linked suppression is a strong preclinical principle and a useful therapeutic objective, but it is not yet a validated clinical mechanism. Trials should combine product characterization and tracking with linkage-dependent assays, tissue analysis, donor-versus-third-party testing, and protocolized immunosuppression reduction.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

articles.title: Inflammation Induced Immune Suppression: Implications in Immune Regulation and Tumor Immunity.
articles.abstract: NA: The inflammatory process is a fundamentally conserved component of host defense, naturally intended to eliminate pathogens and repair damaged tissue. However, unresolved, persistent inflammation triggers immune regulatory pathways which attempt to maintain homeostasis by suppressing immune cell activities. Hence, the intended protective aspect of inflammatory response is gradually subverted into a state of compromised host immunity. While chronic inflammation directly promotes tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance, the resulting inflammation induced immune suppression further facilitates cancer progression by evading immune surveillance. Tumor cells, surrounding stromal cells, infiltrating immune cells, and metabolic mediators generate continuous inflammatory signals which can activate interconnected signaling pathways involving NF-κB, STAT3, mTOR etc. These pathways promote the recruitment and functional activation of specialized immunosuppressive cell types, including myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), regulatory T cells (Tregs), regulatory B cells (Bregs), and neutrophils. Chronic inflammation also contributes to T cell exhaustion, the upregulation of immune checkpoints, and metabolic competition, all of which hinder effective antitumor immunity. Advanced technological approaches using relevant preclinical models have started to reveal the complex nature of suppressive immune cell populations, their development, and expose previously unrecognized therapeutic targets. Here, the role of different suppressive immune and non-immune cells, pathways, and key mediators that are induced under inflammation and coordinatively generate and maintain an immunosuppressive state in cancer has been extensively discussed. Furthermore, the therapeutic possibilities of targeting these interconnected mechanisms for improving antitumor immunity and its related challenges have been reviewed. This overview of inflammation-driven immune-suppression may be further relevant for the understanding and management of other related immune disorders.

articles.title: Maternal thyroid status and immune adaptation at the maternal-fetal interface: distinguishing direct from indirect pathways.
articles.abstract: NA: Pregnancy depends on coordinated endocrine and immune adaptation to support fetal tolerance, antimicrobial defense, trophoblast invasion, and vascular remodeling. Maternal thyroid dysfunction is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, but serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and free thyroxine (FT4) do not define T4/T3 exposure in placental or decidual cells. This Mini Review examines direct and indirect immune pathways, distinguishing maternal thyroid status from local thyroid hormone (TH) transport and metabolism, receptor-dependent signaling, and thyroid autoimmunity. Placental hormone handling has the strongest experimental support: MCT8/MCT10 and DIO2/DIO3 regulate local availability, although much of the transport evidence comes from term placentas. Human trophoblast and endometrial or decidual stromal studies suggest context-dependent effects on decidualization and trophoblast behavior. These responses could affect immune adaptation indirectly through changes in the immune, metabolic, and vascular niche. Evidence for direct TH effects on uterine natural killer (uNK) cells and decidual macrophages remains limited and gestational-age dependent. Direct evidence for decidual regulatory or effector T cells and dendritic cells is lacking, and many proposed mechanisms come from animal or nonpregnant settings. The available data do not support a single TH-driven immune phenotype or establish whether maternal thyroid status acts mainly through immune cells or surrounding tissues. Studies combining paired blood and interface tissue, longitudinal sampling, local T3/T4 measurements, pathway-specific perturbation, and human multicellular models are needed to test both routes and connect hormone supply and metabolism with immune and vascular function. Thyroid autoimmunity should be analyzed separately from local TH receptor signaling.

articles.title: Combined Prognostic Value of Treg Cells, CRP, APTT, and Fibrinogen in Sepsis Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to analyze the correlation between CD3+T cells, Treg cells, APTT, FIB, and CRP in patients with sepsis to explore the predictive value of these combined indicators for the prognosis of sepsis patients.
METHODS: Clinical data were retrospectively collected to compare CD3+T cells, Treg cells, APTT, PT, FIB, D-dimer, CRP, PCT, and PLT levels between the septic shock group and non-septic shock group, as well as between the non-survivors group and the survivors group. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted, and the area under the curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the predictive value of Treg cell, APTT, FIB, and CRP levels for prognosis in sepsis patients. Spearman correlation analysis was used to examine the associations between CD3+T cells, Treg cells, FIB, APTT, and CRP levels in sepsis patients and between Treg cells and ALT, AST, TBIL, DBIL, and IBIL levels.
RESULTS: Treg cells, FIB, APTT, and CRP were used to predict sepsis mortality, the corresponding AUCs were 0.779, 0.635, 0.756, and 0.720. The combined AUC was 0.851, outperforming each single marker.
CONCLUSION: Treg cells, FIB, APTT, and CRP levels correlate with the severity of sepsis. The combined use of these four indicators demonstrates promising predictive value for sepsis prognosis.

articles.title: Remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment and underlying oncogenic molecular mechanisms in HPV-associated OSCC.
articles.abstract: NA: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) possesses unique clinical and biological characteristics, while its specific clinicopathological features and underlying immune-molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically characterize the clinicopathological traits of HPV-associated OSCC and elucidate the key molecular and immune regulatory axes driving its malignant progression. We retrospectively analyzed the correlations between HPV infection status and multiple clinical parameters including age, gender, primary tumor location, clinical stage, pathological grade, and 5-year overall survival (OS) in OSCC patients. IHC was performed to detect the protein expression levels of p53, Cyclin D1 and pRb in OSCC tumor tissues, while flow cytometry was used to quantify the infiltration levels of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) and regulatory T cells (Tregs) in paired tumor tissues and peripheral blood specimens. Integrated transcriptomic RNA sequencing, miRNA target prediction and bioinformatic analyses were further conducted to screen core oncogenic immune targets and specific regulatory pathways in HPV-positive OSCC. Significant differences in primary tumor site, pathological differentiation and 5-year OS were identified between HPV-positive and HPV-negative OSCC patients, with no notable differences in age, gender and clinical stage across groups. And HPV-positive OSCC tissues presented markedly downregulated p53 and Cyclin D1 expression compared with the HPV-negative counterpart. MDSC levels progressively increased from controls to patients with oral precancerous lesions and OSCC, whereas Treg levels were significantly elevated in OSCC patients compared with both controls and patients with precancerous lesions. Bioinformatic analysis revealed that Calsequestrin 2 (CASQ2) expression was negatively correlated with tumor purity in HPV-positive OSCC, and two core circRNA-miRNA regulatory axes (hsa_circ_0058495/hsa-miR-2115-5p and hsa_circ_0032029/hsa-miR-2115-5p) were identified to target CASQ2 specifically. Collectively, HPV infection remodels the OSCC tumor microenvironment into an immunosuppressive phenotype via inducing abnormal accumulation of MDSCs and Tregs, thereby promoting OSCC malignant progression. The miRNA-mediated CASQ2 dysregulation may serve as a core pathogenic driver of HPV-positive OSCC. These findings uncover a novel immune-molecular mechanism underlying HPV-associated OSCC progression, and provide a theoretical basis for stratified precision immunotherapy for this unique OSCC subtype.

articles.title: Controversies and consensus on immune function and long-term health risks following adult thymectomy: a comprehensive review of molecular mechanisms and real-world evidence.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term immunological, oncological, and clinical consequences of adult thymectomy by synthesizing recent basic, translational, and real-world clinical evidence.
BACKGROUND: Historical surgical paradigms regarded the post-pubertal adult thymus as an immunologically redundant, fatty involuted organ, justifying routine "incidental" resection during cardiac procedures. A high-profile 2023 cohort study in The New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM) challenged this concept, reporting that adult thymectomy significantly increased 5-year all-cause mortality and cancer risk. Subsequent population-level studies (US SEER/NCDB, French PMSI) and deep-learning imaging cohorts have sparked debate, offering both corroborating and conflicting insights into adult thymic function.
METHODS AND SYNTHESIS: This review synthesizes cellular mechanisms (TREC dynamics, TCR repertoire contraction, senescence-associated T cells, Treg lineage stability) and endocrine factors (thymulin-mediated myeloid regulation) with clinical data stratified by age at surgery, indication, resection extent, and follow-up duration.
CONCLUSIONS: The adult thymus remains functionally active, exporting naïve T cells and humoral immunomodulators like thymulin that maintain peripheral immune tolerance and restrain inflammaging. Clinical evaluation must differentiate between incidental resection (which induces avoidable iatrogenic immunosenescence) and therapeutic resection (e.g., for thymic epithelial tumors or myasthenia gravis), where removing a diseased, immunosuppressive microenvironment can reduce secondary cancer risk. Partial thymectomy (PT) is emerging as an option to preserve immunocompetence when oncologically feasible.

articles.title: Cardio-immune crosstalk in novel radioimmunotherapy: implications for tumor immune remodeling, radiosensitization, and cardiac safety.
articles.abstract: NA: Emerging radiotherapy modalities are reshaping cancer treatment by combining improved physical dose delivery with distinct immunobiological effects. FLASH radiotherapy, boron neutron capture therapy, spatially fractionated/lattice radiotherapy, proton and carbon-ion radiotherapy, and immunomodulatory stereotactic body radiotherapy can promote immunogenic cell death, innate immune sensing, antigen presentation, and effector lymphocyte responses, but may also induce checkpoint signaling, suppressive myeloid programs, regulatory T-cell activity, and other mechanisms of adaptive radioresistance. As these approaches are increasingly integrated with immunotherapy, their therapeutic window should be defined not only by tumor control but also by immune-mediated effects in normal tissues. This review focuses on cardio-immune crosstalk as an underexplored dimension of novel radioimmunotherapy, particularly in thoracic malignancies. We discuss how pathways that support tumor radiosensitization-including cGAS-STING-type I interferon signaling, myeloid-stromal remodeling, and checkpoint-regulated T-cell activation-may also perturb cardiac immune homeostasis after cardiac radiation exposure and systemic immune activation. We further examine how radiation modality, spatial dose distribution, dose rate, and cardiac substructure exposure may modify this balance. Direct characterization of cardiac immune responses remains limited for several emerging radiotherapy modalities, highlighting an important translational gap. Finally, we propose an integrated tumor-blood-heart framework combining tumor-response biomarkers, systemic immune profiling, and markers of cardiac vulnerability for future risk stratification and longitudinal assessment. This framework is conceptual and requires prospective clinical validation. Defining tissue-specific immune responses may help optimize novel radioimmunotherapy to maximize durable antitumor immunity while preserving cardiovascular safety.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

articles.title: Regulatory T cells in the bone marrow microenvironment: homeostatic crosstalk, disease remodeling, and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: NA: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) help maintain immune balance in hematopoietic niches by interacting with the bone marrow microenvironment. Under normal conditions, surrounding cells send signals that affect Treg movement, their length of stay in the bone marrow, their number and activity. In turn, Tregs affect hematopoietic stem cells, mesenchymal stromal cells, and other immune cells through direct contact or factors they release. When this balance is disturbed, Treg numbers and functions may change according to the disease condition, and these changes are related to the development and progression of multiple myeloma, myelodysplastic syndromes, acute myeloid leukemia, aplastic anemia, and immune thrombocytopenia. Epigenetic changes and other molecular abnormalities may further disturb this communication and allow the abnormal state to continue. Current investigational treatment methods mainly aim to increase Treg numbers, selectively remove certain Tregs, or adjust their functions by targeting the bone marrow environment. This review summarizes existing evidence about these interactions, explains how they become abnormal, and discusses their potential value in restoring normal blood cell production and immune balance.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

articles.title: Cancer immunotherapy and mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: NA: The complexity of the tumor microenvironment often leads to resistance to cancer immunotherapy, and mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming is an important mechanism underlying tumor immune evasion. Treatment selection and response prediction remain challenging because the mechanisms of resistance and changes in the tumor immune microenvironment are incompletely understood. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of immunotherapy resistance will facilitate the development of targeted strategies to overcome resistance. This review synthesizes the manifestations and consequences of mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming in tumor cells and summarizes how tumor-derived metabolites shape an immunosuppressive TME. It focuses on how mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming in antitumor immune cells, including CD8+ T cells, dendritic cells, M1-like tumor-associated macrophages, and natural killer cells, and in immunosuppressive cells, including regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and M2-like tumor-associated macrophages, contributes to the exhaustion of antitumor immunity and promotes tumor immune evasion. This review examines how mitochondrial metabolism can be targeted to overcome immunotherapy resistance and summarizes the mechanisms and current status of related immunotherapeutic strategies. It also discusses the current bottlenecks and future directions of metabolism-targeted cancer immunotherapy. Overall, this review not only elucidates the mechanisms by which mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming drives tumor immune evasion but also provides a theoretical basis for optimizing metabolism-targeted immunotherapy.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

articles.title: Glutaminase Isoenzyme and Splice-Variant Remodeling in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Redox Vulnerability, Ferroptosis, and Therapeutic Resistance.
articles.abstract: NA: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remodels glutamine metabolism within a liver often affected by fibrosis and impaired metabolic reserve. Rather than treating total GLS1 expression as a surrogate for dependency, this review examines how GLS isoform composition (GAC/KGA) and glutamate routing between alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent anaplerosis and glutathione-associated redox defense may influence ferroptosis and treatment response. EGFR-AKT-WTAP-mediated splicing favors GAC, whereas S100A14-mediated GLS/KGA stabilization contributes to sorafenib resistance in selected HCC models. The GAC-associated NADPH phenotype is indirect: glutaminase does not itself produce NADPH. Splice-switching ASO5 has shown proof of concept in HCC cells and locally treated xenografts, but systemic delivery and clinical relevance are untested. GOT2 loss and treatment-induced ASNS alter preclinical responses to CB-839. GLS2 has tumor-suppressive, pro-tumor metabolic and catalysis-independent functions in different experimental settings; GLS1-high/GLS2-low remodeling is also present in nonmalignant chronic liver disease. Human HCC spatial studies now link ammonia-rich niches to regulatory T-cell enrichment, although GLS1-specific ammonia causality remains unresolved. Future development requires isoform-aware patient selection, direct target-engagement measurements and liver and immune safety monitoring.

articles.title: Transcriptomic identification of mitophagy-related plaque markers HAND2, NRP1 and RNF213, with external replication and in vivo validation of MLXIP.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, and mitophagy dysfunction contributes to its pathogenesis. However, the mitophagy-related molecular signatures that could serve as plaque-associated markers remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: Paired differential expression analysis of GSE43292 (32 plaque vs. 32 paired macroscopically intact carotid samples), combined with weighted gene co-expression network analysis, defined a plaque-associated module that was intersected with 4,922 mitophagy-associated genes (GeneCards) to identify mitophagy-related DEGs. LASSO, Random Forest and XGBoost were applied as an auxiliary, patient-grouped, cross-validated feature-selection step; a logistic-regression model fitted on the shared genes was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). External validation used GSE100927 (69 plaque vs. 35 control peripheral artery samples). Immune infiltration was assessed by CIBERSORT, and MLXIP protein abundance was explored by Western blot in a small ApoE⁻/⁻ murine model. Comparator specimens were macroscopically intact tissue (Stary types I-II).
RESULTS: Paired analysis of GSE43292 identified 1,249 differentially expressed genes, of which 107 were mitophagy-related. Patient-grouped machine-learning feature selection nominated three consensus markers-HAND2, NRP1 and RNF213-and a three-gene logistic-regression model reached an out-of-fold area under the curve (AUC) of 0.892 (95% CI 0.810-0.973); because selection and evaluation used the same cohort, these results are exploratory. All three were directionally reproduced in the independent external cohort GSE100927 (direction-locked AUC 0.814, 0.942 and 0.848 respectively). Of three genes examined a priori, MLXIP and EPB41L4A-AS1 replicated in the external cohort (AUC 0.834 for both), whereas RNU4ATAC did not (AUC 0.321). CIBERSORT showed higher macrophage and memory B-cell fractions and lower regulatory T-cell fractions in plaques. In an exploratory in vivo experiment (n = 3 per group), aortic MLXIP protein was 37.7-fold higher in atherosclerotic mice than in controls (P = 0.11) with unchanged MLXIP mRNA; these data were directional only.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, bioinformatics and machine learning nominated HAND2, NRP1 and RNF213 as candidate mitophagy-related plaque markers, with MLXIP and EPB41L4A-AS1 replicated in an independent cohort, and pointed to a mitophagy-immune axis in plaque pathogenesis. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Combined inhibition of BCL2 activity and CD28 signaling to prevent graft-versus-host disease.
articles.abstract: NA: Post-transplantation cyclophosphamide (PTCy)-based prophylaxis has become one of the most widely used strategies to prevent graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), particularly after HLA-haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Well-tolerated GVHD prophylaxis regimens beyond PTCy are needed, because adverse events associated with Cy administration, such as cardiac toxicity, remain a safety concern. Costimulation blockade using abatacept (ABA) is an established complementary strategy to improve GVHD prevention without a calcineurin inhibitor. Here, we investigated venetoclax (VEN), a selective B-cell leukemia/lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) inhibitor, as a candidate partner with ABA to prevent GVHD. In a murine MHC-haploidentical HCT model, we demonstrate that prevention of GVHD with a combination of short-term VEN and CD28 costimulation blockade using ABA (VEN+ABA) was comparable to that with Cy+ABA and superior to that with Cy monotherapy, while maintaining GVL effects. Flow cytometry analysis revealed a higher regulatory T (Treg)/conventional T (Tcon) ratio with the VEN+ABA combination compared to Cy+ABA. Using donor CD8+ alloreactive TCR-transgenic T cells, we show that the VEN+ABA combination produced a prominent cleaved caspase-3 signature only in allo-activated T cells, and cells from the spleen at day 9 after HCT with VEN+ABA did not respond after ex vivo CD3/CD28 stimulation. Collectively, our study supports a VEN+ABA GVHD prophylaxis strategy associated with preferential apoptosis of alloreactive T cells while preserving GVL activity to replace alkylator-based prophylaxis.

articles.title: Cross-Species Single-Cell, Single-Nucleus, and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal Remodeling Features of the Immune Microenvironment and Tissue Architecture Associated With Prostate Aging and Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
articles.abstract: NA: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is closely associated with advancing age, but the tissue, cellular, and molecular features associated with prostate aging and BPH remain incompletely understood. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from Homo sapiens (Hsa) and Mus musculus (Mmu), single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data from Macaca fascicularis (Mfa), and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data from Hsa to characterize prostate remodeling across the available age groups. Cross-species integration using one-to-one ortholog mapping and scGen-based batch correction generated a prostate atlas comprising 47 samples and more than 400,000 cells. In species-specific analyses, CD4_Tem, CD4_Treg, CD8_CTL, Macro_IL1B, and Macro_LYVE1 were more abundant in Middle-aged or Old groups. These populations exhibited diverse pathway signatures related to inflammation, angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. In addition, basal, club, and hillock cells exhibited higher scores for EMT-related transcriptional features and features associated with ECM remodeling in Old Hsa and Old Mmu groups. Fibro_IL1R1, Fibro_C7, and SMC_CNN1 were more abundant in Old Hsa and Old Mmu groups, with higher activity of pathways related to inflammation and ECM remodeling. Tip endothelial cells were more abundant in Old Hsa and Old Mmu groups, with higher angiogenesis-related pathway activity, whereas venous endothelial cells had higher activity of pathways related to inflammation and ECM remodeling. In summary, our study characterizes remodeling features of the immune microenvironment and tissue architecture associated with prostate aging and BPH across species.

articles.title: Probiotic-based sequential delivery system for gut-brain co-therapy against inflammatory bowel disease-associated anxiety/depression.
articles.abstract: NA: With the emergence of the gut-brain axis, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is no longer simply regarded as a localized intestinal disease but as a systemic disorder intimately associated with psychiatric comorbidities, including anxiety and depression. However, conventional therapeutic strategies predominantly target localized colonic inflammation, which often yields suboptimal outcomes. This highlights a critical need for gut-brain co-therapy to achieve comprehensive IBD management. Based on our observation that indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) possesses the potential to attenuate hippocampal neuroinflammation and subsequently modulate intestinal inflammation via the acetylcholine pathway, we engineered a gut-brain co-therapy delivery platform (CB-ASA/IAA/L). This system comprises Clostridium butyricum (CB) loaded with 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA), encapsulated by a pH-responsive Eudragit L100-55 layer incorporating IAA. This microecological preparation is based on effective protection and delivery of CB, achieving the delivery of IAA to the brain and 5-ASA to the colon simultaneously. This sequential-release delivery system achieved intestinal barrier repair, promoted macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype, and restored Th17/Treg balance to recover intestinal homeostasis, while simultaneously alleviating anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in colitis mice. Importantly, the system demonstrated a robust ability to prevent inflammatory recurrence, a major clinical challenge in IBD treatment. This research offers a new avenue for the effective treatment of IBD-associated anxiety/depression by coordinating neuroimmune modulation with local intestinal repair.

articles.title: Disrupting the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia: Mechanism of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction in the treatment of ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: NA: Our previous studies have shown that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively suppresses central immune-inflammatory responses, modulates peripheral inflammatory mediators, reduces the infiltration of peripheral T lymphocytes into the central nervous system, and promotes the conversion of infiltrated T lymphocytes in the brain into Treg cells. However, whether Huanglian Jiedu Decoction can influence M2 microglial polarization by regulating T-lymphocyte phenotypic transformation and thereby modulate neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke remains unclear. This study focused on Treg-mediated microglial polarization to investigate the potential of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction to modulate interactions between T lymphocytes and microglia in the treatment of ischemic stroke. We established a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion, an inflammatory model of Jurkat T cells stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate and ionomycin, and a Transwell co-culture model of T lymphocytes and HMC3 microglia. The results showed that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively alleviated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model of middle cerebral artery, inhibited central inflammatory responses, and promoted the polarization of microglia toward the M2 phenotype. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction also promoted the conversion of CD4+ T cells in brain tissue into regulatory T cells and regulated regulatory T cells through the interleukin-10/Janus kinase 1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 pathway, thereby promoting the activation of M2 microglia. These findings suggest that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction, which has heat-clearing and detoxifying properties, can regulate immune homeostasis, inhibit secondary neuroinflammation associated with ischemic stroke, and exert neuroprotective effects. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction may therefore treat ischemic stroke by modulating the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia, providing a traditional Chinese medicine-based strategy for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

articles.title: From broad suppression to precision targeting: the new era of antigen-specific immunotherapy for type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: NA: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by the selective destruction of pancreatic β-cells driven by autoreactive immune responses. In recent decades, the global incidence of T1D has risen markedly, with the most rapid increase observed among children and adolescents, imposing a substantial burden on healthcare systems worldwide. Conventional treatment primarily relies on exogenous insulin administration, which manages hyperglycemia but does not address the underlying autoimmune pathology or restore endogenous insulin production. Antigen-specific immunotherapy (ASI) has emerged as a promising strategy that may restore antigen-specific immune tolerance via multiple mechanisms, including clonal deletion/ anergy, immune deviation, induction of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and type 1 regulatory T (Tr1) cells, and tolerogenic antigen presentation. ASI may help preserve residual β-cell function and potentially modify disease progression. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in ASI for T1D, with a focus on the biological features of key T1D autoantigens, optimization of antigen delivery strategies, and prospects for clinical translation.

articles.title: Immune Mechanisms of Oral Tolerance in the Prevention of IgE-Mediated Food Allergy.
articles.abstract: NA: IgE-mediated food allergy develops when the immune response to dietary antigens is diverted from active tolerance towards a pathogenic type 2 immune response. Oral tolerance is the default, antigen-specific suppression of immune responses to ingested proteins. Early introduction trials, most notably the LEAP study, have demonstrated that oral exposure to food antigens during the first year of life can prevent food allergy and generate durable tolerance. Mechanistic advances have revealed that oral tolerance is governed by the coordinated activity of multiple overlapping immune layers. These include transcellular antigen transport through goblet cell-associated antigen passages (GAPs), tolerogenic antigen presentation by specialized RORγt+ antigen presenting cells (APCs) and classical dendritic cells (cDCs), induction and maintenance of heterogeneous regulatory T cell programs, and germinal center regulation of IgE and IgG responses. These cellular programs are further modulated by genetic determinants including HLA class II alleles, filaggrin variants, and microbial metabolites such as butyrate and indole derivatives and non-allergic dietary components. Infections can break tolerance by displacing or reprogramming tolerogenic APCs. Once food allergy has been established, regulatory pathways generated by oral allergen exposure are not sufficient to establish tolerance. These findings support a model in which tolerance and allergy represent competing, self-reinforcing immune states stabilized by redundant regulatory circuits. This review synthesizes the current understanding of these multilayered mechanisms and discusses their implications for prevention and treatment of food allergy.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

articles.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in surgically resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (PRIME-HCC): a prospective, phase 1b, single-arm trial and translational analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab improves survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. We evaluated this combination as neoadjuvant therapy and investigated its effect on peripheral immunity and the tumour microenvironment.
METHODS: PRIME-HCC is a single-arm, phase 1b trial in adults (aged ≥18 years) with early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, Child-Pugh A liver function, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1. Patients received nivolumab (3 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 22 of the first and second cycle) and ipilimumab (1 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of the first cycle only) before liver resection. The primary endpoint was safety, assessed by treatment-related delays to surgery and adverse events in the intention-to-treat population. Translational analyses included imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on paired tumour samples, peripheral immunophenotyping, T-cell receptor (TCR) β sequencing, and longitudinal tumour-agnostic circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) profiling. This trial was registered with EudraCT (2018-000987-27) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03682276); follow-up is currently ongoing.
FINDINGS: Between Sept 18, 2019, and Sept 28, 2023, of 43 patients assessed for eligibility, 33 patients were enrolled (25 [76%] male and 8 [24%] female; median age 68 years [range 38-80; IQR 63-73]); median follow-up was 25·7 months (95% CI 21·2-30·1). Any-grade adverse events occurred in 31 (94%) of patients, with treatment-related adverse events (trAEs) in 25 (76%) patients. Grade 3 trAEs occurred in three (9%) patients (transaminase elevation, anaemia, and dyspnoea). Serious adverse events were recorded in three (9%) patients, and no grade 4-5 events or treatment-related deaths occurred. 30 (91%) patients underwent surgery, including two (6%) who had immune checkpoint inhibitor-related surgical delays. Objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 was noted in eight (25%; 95% CI 13-42) patients (one complete response and seven partial responses), with 31 (97%; 84-100) patients achieving disease control. The absence of ctDNA after surgery was associated with improved 2-year recurrence-free survival (nine [82%] of 11 patients vs two [29%] of seven; p=0·049), as was at least 50% ctDNA reduction (median not reached [95% CI not reached] vs 20·9 months [95% CI 16·3-25·4]; HR 0·14 [95% CI 0·02-0·91]; p=0·039). Patients with objective responses showed expansion of peripheral PD-1-positive, Ki-67-positive, CD8-positive T cells (T-responding exhausted cells [Tresp]), associated with higher baseline intratumoral progenitor-exhausted T cells (Tpex) and increased Tresp infiltration. Patients whose disease did not respond to treatment exhibited enrichment of terminally exhausted CD8-positive T cells (Tex-term; CD8-positive PD-1-positive TOX-positive cells) and regulatory T cells.
INTERPRETATION: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab is feasible in early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and later-phase randomised trials are needed to confirm the efficacy of this treatment strategy. Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring could support detection of minimal residual disease and warrants further prospective validation.
